universal_lens: Practice-window temporal dynamics and open-media signal processing define pre-official-status betting edges via location-velocity kinematics. The universal lens unifies spatial kinematics, probabilistic tackle fields, and outcome distributions into a single measure-theoretic framework. By treating player trajectories as stochastic processes on a bounded manifold, we map continuous physical states to discrete event probabilities using kernel-weighted similarity operators.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updating on practice-period telemetry using GSI's conformal predictive distributions over player availability states. GSI employs Bayesian hierarchical modeling over the CRPS-optimized yardage distributions, utilizing conformal inference to generate rigorous prediction intervals for play outcomes. Similarity kernels weight historical priors, dynamically adjusting for contextual covariates like down-and-distance while strictly preventing temporal data leakage.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions in GSE model driven by open-media drill sequences and positional velocity thresholds. GSE translates these primitives into real-time state-transition matrices, evaluating Void Improvement Scores and fractional tackle probabilities to quantify defensive effort. The engine continuously updates situational awareness by integrating causal uplift from pre-snap motion into dynamic expected points models.

primitives.verbatim_quote: What matters is location and velocity, not whether someone "looked good." - Helmet in hand, standing with trainers, or on the side rehab field while the position group works is a real limitation.
primitives.assumptions: Player movement during open media periods correlates with official participation status; velocity and location are sufficient to infer participation eligibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When v < threshold, player is classified as non-participatory.

primitives.verbatim_quote: The window is often minutes, not hours, and it is largest on Wednesday of a short week or when a star's status is still priced as a coin flip.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal proximity between open media and official reporting defines critical decision window; probability of status change increases near deadline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Δt < 10 mins implies high sensitivity to open media signals.

primitives.name: Drill Sequence Signal

primitives.breakdown_regime: If S(n) = full-speed → S(n+1) = 11-on-11, then status = full.

primitives.name: Continuous Ranked Probability Score Yardage Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: CRPS evaluation for yardage distribution (CDF from –99 to 99 yards, non-decreasing).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F(y): Predicted Cumulative Distribution Function (dimensionless), H: Heaviside step function (dimensionless), Y_obs: Observed yardage gain (yards), y: Integration variable (yards)

primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if extreme outlier plays exceed the [-99, 99] boundary or if the predictive model outputs non-probabilistic point estimates.

primitives.name: Fractional Tackle Success Field
primitives.verbatim_quote: Tackling probability fields (2024 theme) used physics-based fractional tackles or XGBoost for success probability (>75% threshold for missed tackle credit).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(T|x): Probability of tackle given feature vector x (dimensionless), \sigma: Sigmoid activation function, f_k: k-th decision tree in ensemble (dimensionless), x: Feature vector containing relative positions and velocities (mixed SI units)
primitives.assumptions: Tackle events are conditionally independent given the instantaneous spatial features; XGBoost accurately captures the non-linear interaction of defender proximity and speed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur when tracking data is sparse (e.g., occlusion) or during chaotic pile-ups where individual player vectors lose physical meaning.

layer2.mapping: Derives a continuous risk surface for GSE, allowing the engine to assign fractional credit for defensive pressure even without a completed tackle.

primitives.name: Void Improvement Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: VIS (Void Improvement Score) for coverage effort while ball in air: distance closed by defender during flight (VIS > 0 = erased space; links to EPA/YAC deltas, e.g., high-effort saves ~0.74 EPA).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: VIS: Void Improvement Score (meters), r_d: Defender position vector (meters), r_ball: Ball position vector (meters), t_0: Time of throw (seconds), t_catch: Time of catch/landing (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Defender trajectory is optimally aligned toward the projected ball landing zone; Euclidean distance accurately reflects effective coverage area.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when defenders intentionally backpedal to maintain leverage on route trees, resulting in negative VIS despite optimal positioning.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's effort-to-outcome mapping, directly translating spatial closure into Expected Points Added (EPA) deltas for coaching feedback.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation coefficient between VIS and actual Yards After Catch (YAC) surrendered.

primitives.name: Kernel Weighted Player Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: One key paper uses similarity-based weighting (kNN-like) for projection: similarity r_{ij} between players i and t via kernel on feature vectors x (with averages and penalties); weights w_{ij} incorporating similarity, correlation, or squared terms; predicted outcome ŷ_t = Σ w_{ij} y_i.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_hat_t: Predicted outcome for target player t (dimensionless), y_i: Outcome of historical player i (dimensionless), w_ij: Normalized similarity weight (dimensionless), r_ij: Distance/metric between feature vectors x_i and x_t (dimensionless), K: Kernel function (e.g., Gaussian RBF)
primitives.assumptions: Players with similar kinematic and contextual feature vectors will exhibit similar outcome distributions; the kernel appropriately penalizes dissimilar trajectories.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Curse of dimensionality causes all weights to converge to zero if the feature space x is too high-dimensional without proper regularization.

layer2.mapping: Forms the backbone of GSI's transfer learning module, projecting unknown player capabilities onto known distributions using geometric similarity.
layer2.telemetry: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of projected vs. actual performance metrics for held-out players.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 1 introduces foundational concepts for leveraging pre-official practice reports in football analytics. The core premise is that open media periods—specifically stretching, individual drills, and early team work—are more predictive of final participation status than traditional DNP/limited/full designations. These periods occur before official reports, offering a temporal advantage. The key insight lies in interpreting player location and velocity within these windows rather than relying on subjective 'looks'. A player who spends time on the rehab field or sidelines instead of participating in drills is likely to be designated as limited or out. The timing of this information is crucial; the window is typically minutes, not hours, and expands during uncertain situations like coin-flip statuses. The sequence of drills across Wednesday through Friday provides a longitudinal signal that can be modeled as a state transition process. For example, a player starting with individual-only work and ending with full 11-on-11 reps suggests readiness. Conversely, a pattern of skipping team periods even after individual work indicates continued limitation. This chapter emphasizes that the edge comes not from secret information but from superior interpretation of publicly available data streams. The interplay between temporal dynamics, physical behavior, and coaching language creates a rich dataset for probabilistic modeling and predictive inference.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical foundation of this chapter window rests on the transition from deterministic Newtonian mechanics to stochastic process theory applied to American football. We begin by defining the state space of a play as a high-dimensional manifold parameterized by the $(X, Y, S)$ coordinates of all 22 active agents. The 'Zoo' approach simplifies this by projecting these vectors relative to the passer, effectively reducing the degrees of freedom and isolating the core geometric interactions between rushers and blockers.

From this reduced state space, we derive the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) as the primary loss function. Unlike Mean Squared Error, which only penalizes deviations in the mean, CRPS evaluates the entire cumulative distribution function (CDF) of potential yardage gains. This is crucial because football outcomes are inherently heavy-tailed and bounded. The integration limits of -99 to 99 yards impose a hard constraint on the manifold, ensuring that the probabilistic forecasts remain physically grounded.

Simultaneously, the introduction of Tackling Probability Fields and Void Improvement Scores (VIS) represents a shift toward continuous-time hazard modeling. By framing a tackle not as a binary event but as a probability field $P(T|\mathbf{x})$ evolving over time, we can quantify defensive effort even when a tackle is evaded. VIS operationalizes this by measuring the rate of change in the Euclidean distance between a defender and the ball trajectory. A positive VIS indicates a reduction in the available phase space for the receiver, directly correlating with negative Expected Points Added (EPA) for the offense.

Finally, the similarity-weighted projection operator provides a non-parametric method to generalize these findings across different players. By employing a kernel function $K(r_{ij})$ on the feature vectors, we construct a weighted average of historical outcomes. This bridges the gap between raw kinematic data and strategic foresight, allowing the system to predict how a specific player's unique physical attributes will interact with the probabilistic fields generated by their opponents.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to early Pythagorean expectation models, which relied solely on aggregate scoring differentials. The advent of Next Gen Stats introduced granular kinematic data, enabling the shift from team-level heuristics to individual player probability fields. The 2020 Big Data Bowl catalyzed the adoption of CRPS and relative coordinate systems, fundamentally altering how we evaluate defensive pressure and spatial control in modern quantitative football analysis.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires inferring latent intent from observable kinematics. A quarterback's pre-snap motion or a receiver's route stem provides causal cues that update the posterior probability of the play design. Our framework treats these actions as deliberate manipulations of the opponent's belief state, aiming to maximize the entropy of the defense's tackling probability field while minimizing the Void Improvement Score achievable by secondary defenders.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Strict anti-collinearity vetoes must be enforced to prevent data leakage, particularly regarding temporal boundaries. Features derived from post-snap outcomes, such as final receiver location, cannot leak into pre-snap motion causal uplift models. Furthermore, we must veto any similarity weights that rely on player identity rather than pure kinematic features to ensure the model generalizes across different rosters and avoids overfitting to star players.

reasoning_traces.think: The chapter establishes that offensive line communication relies on a cascade of visual and neural signals, with each lineman waiting for the previous one to react. This introduces a cumulative propagation delay that can be modeled as a series of exponential decay processes. The core insight is that the center's signal must traverse the entire line, creating a bottleneck that affects both snap timing and defensive anticipation. This primitive is critical for understanding how noise environments (crowd, officials) disrupt this cascade, leading to either premature snaps or delayed reactions. It also forms the basis for analyzing how offenses use variable cadences to mask this delay, trading off coordination for unpredictability.
